docs.text: Как в dev-plan.md: done / partial / greenfield / gated:X.

docs.title: Зафиксированные решения
docs.text:
Приняты в обсуждении, меняют параметры E3:

Параметр Было Стало Почему SEGMENT_SECONDS 900 (15 мин) 60 Окно неподтверждённых сообщений падает с 15 мин до ~1.5; давление на max_ack_pending=150_000 снижается ~15x GRACE_SECONDS — 30 Дозапись опоздавших строк в свой сегмент вместо ошибки Закрытие сегмента start + 900s <= now start + 60s + 30s <= now Учитывает grace Ключ писателя kind (kind, segment_start_ms) Без этого grace не работает: один открытый сегмент на kind вытесняется следующим Владение писателем общий, 2 потока исполнитель на kind Устраняет гонку write_rows vs close_stale ARCHIVER_ACK_WAIT_MS 30_000 120_000 Продление in_progress() ходит раз в 30с при ack_wait 30с — нулевой запас, самостоятельный источник передоставок ARCHIVER_SWEEP_INTERVAL_S 30 30 (без изменений) Рычаг — ack_wait, а не частота sweep Выгрузка в S3 каждый закрытый сегмент суточное слияние, 00:05 UTC ~9 объектов в сутки вместо ~13 000

Обоснование окна риска для суточного слияния: ack привязан к локальной durability (_ack_closed_segment → после fsync + os.replace, лог locally durable+acked), а не к S3. Пока минутки лежат только на диске, второй экземпляр данных — сам стрим: DEFAULT_RETENTION_HOURS = 48, limits-retention, сообщения живут 48ч после ack. Суточное окно = 24ч экспозиции при 48ч возможности перечитать. Сходится с ARCHIVER_MAX_LOCAL_STAGING_DAYS = 2 и с формулой из _check_staging_bound: local_days >= merge_window + verify_lag.

Архиватор остаётся постоянно работающим сервисом. Раз в сутки запускается только этап слияния и выгрузки. Непрерывное потребление md.* и запись минуток остановить нельзя — упрётся max_ack_pending.

docs.title: Волна 1 — архиватор, целостность данных
docs.text: Гейт входа: нет. Критический путь.

docs.title: H1. Писатели по ключу (kind, segment_start_ms), исполнитель на kind
docs.text:
done · archiver/daily_writer.py, archiver/service.py

Сейчас _writers/_segments/_tmp_paths/_final_paths ключуются по kind (скаляр — один открытый сегмент на тип). write_rows идёт в поток через asyncio.to_thread из консьюмера, close_stale — из sweep-цикла, без локов: close_kind может закрыть и переименовать файл ровно во время write_table в другом потоке.

  • Все четыре словаря → ключ (kind, segment_start_ms).
  • _open(kind, day, seg), close_segment(kind, seg); close_stale(now) закрывает все пары, у которых seg + SEGMENT_MS + GRACE_MS <= now.
  • ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) на каждый kind. Все операции писателя для данного kind идут строго в его исполнитель.
  • close_stale и close_all раскладываются на per-kind вызовы, каждый — в свой исполнитель. Иначе sweep продолжит трогать чужие writer'ы и гонка останется на месте.

Приёмка: конкурентный тест «запись + закрытие одного kind» не портит parquet; разные kind пишутся параллельно; close_all на shutdown закрывает всё.

Заметка: _pending_acks уже ключуется (kind, segment_start_ms) — совпадает с новым ключом писателя, дополнительных изменений не требует.

docs.title: H2. Сегмент 60с + grace 30с
docs.text:
done · archiver/daily_writer.py · зависит от H1

  • SEGMENT_SECONDS: 900 → 60, новая GRACE_SECONDS = 30.
  • Условие закрытия: seg + SEGMENT_MS + GRACE_MS <= now.
  • В течение grace одновременно открыты текущий сегмент и предыдущий.

Приёмка: строка с ts внутри grace дозаписывается в свой сегмент, а не в текущий; после grace сегмент закрывается ровно один раз.

docs.title: H3. Запрет воскрешения закрытого сегмента + классификация ошибок
docs.text:
done · archiver/daily_writer.py, archiver/service.py · зависит от H2

Два дефекта, обнаруженные ревью, чинятся здесь.

Дефект 1 — перезапись финализированного сегмента (потеря данных). close_kind делает self._segments.pop(kind, None). После закрытия по sweep состояние очищается, и передоставленное сообщение старого сегмента попадает в ветку «сегмента нет» → _open делает tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True) и создаёт новый writer без проверки, что финальный файл уже существует и выгружен. Следующий os.replace перезаписывает готовый файл одной поздней строкой. В S3 уходит PUT по тому же детерминированному ключу.

Дефект 2 — бесконечная передоставка. Пока сегмент открыт, строка более старого сегмента даёт ValueError("Out-of-order segment"), который ловится в _consume_subject как "transient failure - no ack, will redeliver". Сбой не транзиентный: сегмент укатился вперёд, условие не разрешится никогда.

Правки:

  • Множество закрытых (kind, seg) в памяти + проверка существования финального файла. Переоткрытие закрытого сегмента запрещено.
  • Строка позже grace → msg.term() + archiver_dropped_late_rows_total.
  • Перманентные ошибки (декод, схема, неизвестный kind, слишком поздняя строка) → term(), из передоставки уходят.
  • Транзиентные (диск, S3, брокер) → без ack, передоставка сохраняется.
  • Докстринг _consume_subject («one bad payload can't wedge the subject») привести в соответствие с поведением.

Приёмка: передоставка сообщения уже закрытого сегмента не перезаписывает файл и не зацикливается; счётчик отброшенных растёт; транзиентная ошибка по-прежнему приводит к повтору.

docs.title: H4. ack_wait 30с → 120с
docs.text:
done · archiver/service.py · независима

ARCHIVER_ACK_WAIT_MS: 30_000 → 120_000. При минутных сегментах и grace 30с сообщение висит неподтверждённым ~90с — укладывается почти без продлений, in_progress() становится страховкой для застрявших случаев, а не основным путём.

Цена: после падения архиватора передоставка начнётся через 2 мин вместо 30с. Для архиватора безразлично — он не в торговом пути.

docs.title: H5. Метрики опозданий
docs.text:
partial · common/health.py, archiver/service.py · зависит от H3 (счётчики и snapshot-поля сделаны; Prometheus-экспорт ждёт E6)

  • archiver_late_rows_total{kind} — пришли с опозданием, но в пределах grace, записаны.
  • archiver_dropped_late_rows_total{kind} — позже grace, отброшены.
  • Лаг now - row_ts (gauge или гистограмма) — чтобы на soak увидеть, хватает ли 30 секунд, и подобрать число по факту, а не угадывать.

Приёмка: метрики экспортируются, покрыты тестом.

docs.title: Волна 2 — слияние и выгрузка
docs.text:
Гейт входа: H1-H3.

Путь заливки переписывается: сейчас _archive_closed_file(path) грузит каждый закрытый сегмент сразу.

docs.title: H6. Суточное слияние минуток
docs.text:
done · archiver/merge.py

  • Запуск 00:05 UTC для предыдущих суток. Не 00:00: сегмент 23:59 с grace закрывается в 00:00:30, при старте ровно в полночь он в слияние не попадёт.
  • Берутся только сегменты, для которых start + SEGMENT_MS + GRACE_MS прошло, а не «все файлы в папке за вчера».
  • Потоковая запись: 1440 файлов на kind нельзя собирать в память — читаем по одному, пишем row-group'ами в один ParquetWriter.
  • Та же атомарность, что в close_segment: .tmp + fsync + os.replace.

Приёмка: слитый файл содержит объединение строк; потребление памяти не растёт с числом входных файлов; повторный запуск даёт тот же результат.

docs.title: H7. Выгрузка слитого файла + верификация
docs.text:
done · archiver/s3_sink.py · зависит от H6

Сейчас проверка после PUT — только ContentLength из HEAD. Для дневного файла на десятки мегабайт сверка по длине особенно слаба: побитая передача той же длины пройдёт как успешная.

  • Верификация по ETag или checksum.
  • Минутки удаляются только после успешной верификации.
  • Детерминированный ключ; повторный PUT идемпотентен.

Приёмка: повреждение при передаче детектируется; минутки не удаляются при неуспешной верификации.

docs.title: H8. Идемпотентность и восстановление после крэша
docs.text:
done · archiver/merge.py · зависит от H7

  • Крэш на середине слияния оставляет .tmp, который при старте игнорируется и пересобирается заново.
  • Повторный запуск слияния для того же дня безопасен.
  • Слияние обязано отрабатывать до ARCHIVER_MAX_LOCAL_STAGING_DAYS = 2, иначе получим D9 BREACH вместо выгрузки. Суточное укладывается с запасом.

Приёмка: тест на прерванное слияние; тест на повторный прогон.

docs.title: Волна 3 — остальные блокеры
docs.text: Независимы друг от друга и от волн 1-2, можно параллельно.

docs.title: H9. Запрет отката курсора
docs.text:
done · calc/cursor_store.py

_UPSERT_SQL безусловно перезаписывает stream_seq в том числе меньшим значением — защиты от отката нет.

Через WHERE, а не GREATEST: при GREATEST поле u может разъехаться со stream_seq независимо.

ON CONFLICT (market, symbol, stream_type) DO UPDATE SET ...
  WHERE EXCLUDED.stream_seq > calc_cursor.stream_seq

Плюс счётчик и WARN на попытку отката.

Приёмка: запись меньшего stream_seq не меняет строку; счётчик растёт; u остаётся согласованным со stream_seq.

docs.title: H10. Маскирование секретов в S3Config
docs.text:
done · common/s3_config.py

@dataclass(frozen=True) с key_id/application_key без переопределённого __repr__: любой logger.info("%r", cfg) или traceback выносит креды в лог открытым текстом.

Приёмка: тест, что repr() и f-string форматирование не содержат значений кредов.

docs.title: H11. Алерты + CI-гейт на плейсхолдеры
docs.text:
done · deploy/alerts.yml, CI

Сейчас единственный алерт на лаг консьюмера — > 999999999 с severity: warning, то есть не сработает никогда. Алертов на архиватор, S3 и остановку публикации коллектора нет вообще.

  • Дописать недостающие алерты с теми же TBD-порогами (реальные числа gated:E8 — выводятся из soak, придумать их нельзя).
  • Проверка в CI, запрещающая выкатку конфига с 999999999.

Тогда отсутствие порогов становится видимым блокером, а не тихой дырой.

Приёмка: CI падает на конфиге с плейсхолдером; новые алерты валидны как YAML.

docs.title: Волна 4 — жизненный цикл сервисов и мелкие долги
docs.text: Независимы друг от друга. H12 — гейт для H1: без него закрытие писателей на остановке, ради которого делается волна 1, не выполнится.

docs.title: H12. Обработка SIGTERM во всех трёх сервисах
docs.text:
done · common/service_runner.py · calc/__main__.py, archiver/__main__.py, main.py, trader/service.py · блокирует приёмку H1

asyncio.run(...) без add_signal_handler: по SIGTERM (то есть по docker stop, по рестарту в оркестраторе) корутина не отменяется штатно, и ветка finally с graceful shutdown не отрабатывает. Именно в ней закрываются NATS-соединения, флашатся буферы и — после H1 — закрываются писатели parquet.

Без этого H1 даёт обещание, которого не выполняет: на остановке останутся незакрытые .tmp-файлы, и восстановление ляжет на передоставку вместо штатного закрытия.

  • add_signal_handler(SIGTERM/SIGINT) → отмена главной задачи.
  • Ограниченное время на graceful shutdown, затем принудительный выход.
  • Ненулевой код возврата при аварийной остановке.

Приёмка: SIGTERM приводит к закрытию всех писателей и соединений; тест на отмену главной задачи; .tmp не остаётся.

docs.title: H13. Закрытие NATS-соединения publisher'а в calc
docs.text:
done · calc/bars_publisher.py, calc/service.py

make_bars_publisher(url) открывает собственное соединение (D1: calc не импортирует collector.*), но возвращает только publish — способа закрыть соединение нет. В finally у run_calc_service закрывается только live_nc. Утечка на каждом рестарте сервиса.

Вернуть пару (publish, close) либо async-контекстменеджер; закрывать в том же finally, что и live_nc.

Приёмка: тест, что после остановки сервиса соединение publisher'а закрыто.

docs.title: H14. Потеря бара при ошибке публикации
docs.text:
done · calc/service.py, calc/bars_publisher.py

Upstream обернул publish_bar в except NatsError и отделил транспортные сбои от программных — это улучшение, но бар для закрытого окна всё равно теряется навсегда: следующая итерация цикла строит present_row уже для другого bar_end_ms, повторить публикацию некому.

Решение: ретрай с backoff + метрика + лог.

Ограничение, которое определяет форму ретрая: await publish_bar стоит в последовательном цикле по символам внутри _drive_boundaries. Ретрай «на месте» задержит публикацию всех оставшихся символов того же бара, а при недоступном брокере — умножится на число символов и съест окно целиком. Поэтому ретрай выносится из основного прохода:

  1. Первый проход по символам — без ретрая. Символ, у которого публикация упала с NatsError, складывается в список неотправленных вместе с уже построенным present_row и stamp.
  2. После прохода — повтор только по неотправленным, с экспоненциальным backoff и двумя бюджетами: по числу попыток и по суммарному времени. Оба параметра — в live_config.yaml, не захардкожены (политика CLAUDE.md).
  3. Временной бюджет заведомо меньше периода бара, чтобы ретрай не пересёкся со следующей границей. Стартовые значения: 3 попытки, backoff 0.5/½ с, общий потолок 10 с — estimate,remeasure до E8, как wait_deadline_seconds.
  4. Исчерпан бюджет — бар признаётся потерянным: счётчик + ERROR с symbol, bar_end_ms, числом попыток и последней ошибкой.

Дедуп по Nats-Msg-Id (make_msg_id("binance", symbol, bar_close_ms)) делает повтор безопасным: даже если предыдущая попытка на самом деле дошла, брокер отбросит дубль. То есть ретрай здесь идемпотентен по построению и не может породить второй бар.

Метрики и лог:

  • calc_bars_publish_retries_total{symbol} — сколько повторов потребовалось.
  • calc_bars_publish_failed_total{symbol} — бар потерян после исчерпания бюджета. Это и есть сигнал для алерта (H11).
  • Успех с первой попытки не логируется (сейчас там logger.info на каждый бар); успех после ретрая — WARN с числом попыток; провал — ERROR.

Приёмка: транспортный сбой с последующим восстановлением приводит к доставке бара, а не к потере; retries_total растёт; исчерпание бюджета даёт failed_total + ERROR; ретрай одного символа не задерживает публикацию остальных сверх временного бюджета; повторная публикация того же (symbol, bar_close_ms) не создаёт дубль в стриме.

docs.title: H15. Пин верхней границы prometheus_client
docs.text:
done · requirements.txt

prometheus_client>=0.20 без верхней границы, тогда как соседние записи запинены (psycopg[binary]>=3.1,<4). Мажорное обновление приедет молча.

Приёмка: версия ограничена сверху по конвенции файла.

docs.title: H16. Откат cutover в deploy_order
docs.text:
done · deploy/deploy_order.py

Есть cutover и retire, но нет закодированного действия отката для отмены cutover на середине: оператор поднимает stop-first сервис руками, без fail-loud защиты. При числе открытых блокеров в контуре вероятность отката на проде не теоретическая.

Структура модуля это позволяет: SERVICE_DEPLOY_POLICY — данные, deploy_plan — чистая функция от политики, assert_stop_first/_unknown_service уже дают fail-loud. Добавить обратный план тем же приёмом.

Приёмка: план отката выводится из той же политики; неверный порядок отката невыразим.

docs.title: H17. metrics_source — дефолт внутрь config.py
docs.text:
done · trader/config.py, main.py

Поле nullable, дефолт None → "inprocess" разрешается в main.py:42 (cfg.metrics_source or "inprocess"), то есть вне config.py. При невалидном значении _coerce падает корректно, но отсутствующее подставляется молча — расходится с политикой CLAUDE.md «падать громко» и с докстрингом LiveConfig, который утверждает «All fields are required».

Само послабление сделано осознанно (совместимость старых конфигов при выкатке, комментарий в _FIELDS), поэтому задача не «запретить», а перенести разрешение дефолта в LiveConfig.load() и поправить докстринг — чтобы дефолт был один и в одном месте.

Связано: metrics_source — временный флаг переходного периода inprocess/bars без зафиксированного условия исчезновения. Условие снятия стоит записать здесь же, вместе с флагом present_only (см. «Вне скоупа»): оба снимаются одним решением.

Приёмка: дефолт разрешается внутри config.py; докстринг соответствует поведению; main.py не содержит подстановки.

docs.title: Порядок и зависимости
docs.text:
H12 ─(гейт приёмки)─┐
                    ↓
       H1 → H2 → H3 → H5
                  ↓
            H6 → H7 → H8

H4, H9, H10, H11, H13, H14, H15, H16, H17 — независимы

Волна 1 (H1-H5) — критический путь, закрывает потерю и порчу данных. Волна 2 (H6-H8) — можно начинать после H3. Волна 3 (H9-H11) — параллельно в любой момент. Волна 4 (H12-H17) — параллельно, но H12 делается раньше приёмки H1: без обработки SIGTERM закрытие писателей на остановке, ради которого затевается волна 1, не выполняется.

Рекомендуемый порядок старта: H12 → H1 → H2 → H3, дальше по готовности.

docs.title: Проверка на каждом шаге
docs.text:
Baseline на 2a78111: 1972 passed, 26 skipped, 1 xfailed (~14 мин, исключая tests/test_alpha_mining_dsr_gate.py — падает на импорте из-за отсутствующего sklearn, к изменениям отношения не имеет).

Каждая задача: python -m compileall -q по затронутым файлам + целевые тесты; перед коммитом — полный сьют и сверка с baseline.

docs.title: Вне скоупа PR #97
docs.text:
• Дискриминатор для stats. 4 RawDataKind (open_interest, taker_ratio, long_short_ratio, market_stats) мапятся на один stats.parquet; _normalise_columns ветвится только по trades/klines/funding/markprice. Код сам помечает это как «UNION over ~5 aliased poller shapes with NO on-wire discriminator — UNRESOLVED ambiguity». Нужна смена проводного контракта через три сервиса с версионированием и порядком выкатки. Отдельный эпик.
  • Reconnect для консьюмера баров. Эфемерные подписки выжинаются по InactiveThreshold; replay выполняется только на бутстрапе, поэтому после длительного разрыва бары могут тихо перестать приходить. Рестарт при этом покрыт: connect_bars прогоняет replay_bars_on_boot и открывает живые подписки с opt_start_seq = last_replayed + 1, дедуп по (symbol, bar_ts) гасит перекрытие. Требует проверки поведения nats-py на переподключении.
  • Design-долг (из второго прохода ревью): разнесение common/nats_wire.py на streams/subjects (fan-in 12, три слоя в одном модуле); check_stream_invariants → diff_stream_invariants (перекос CQS); _pending_acks → тип PendingAckBuffer; GateThresholds без дефолтов + именованная фабрика tbd_soak_placeholder(); удаление флага present_only (легаси-ветка недостижима в проде); разделение common/health.py.
  • Компакция за пределами суток — если понадобится, отдельной задачей.

docs.title: soak-runbooks.md — reproducible procedures (human runs; no product code here)
S-1. Occupancy + S2 precise (closes max_bytes byte value)
docs.text:
1. Предусловия: compose с NATS 2.10, контур usdm 60 символов (прод-профиль default_stream_names), streams по контракту (48h + max_bytes-orientir).
  2. Лить живой поток ≥48h (или ≥7d для пика/перекоса). Раз в час снимать: stream_info (messages/bytes/first_seq/last_seq per stream), docker system df -v SIZE тома nats_data, du file-store (где доступно).
  3. S2 = disk_bytes / logical_bytes за то же окно (метод X-002 в research-notes.md; races sealed-рекомпрессии усреднять).
  4. Выход: daily_wire_peak (не среднее), s2_ratio, overhead; max_bytes = peak × 2d × s2 × 1.2; daily-merge размер (проверка «слитое легче», Q-005(b) условие).

docs.title: S-2. Kill-archiver (JetStream + files; INV-003 gate step 6)
docs.text:
1. Остановить archiver-durable (НЕ трогать FileWriter/трейдер). Держать > max_age.
  2. Наблюдать: диск JetStream стоит на max_bytes (publish НЕ блокируется, discard-old), файловые тома — в границе §transition-plan step 2 п.3; quality-stamp gap + num_pending алерт срабатывают (громкая дыра).
  3. Критерий: стоящий диск + громкая дыра + живой publish. Иначе — шаг 6 запрещён, чинить и повторять.

docs.title: S-3. Peak capture (volatile session, multi-hour)
docs.text:
1. Покрыть волатильную сессию захватом wire-rate (метод X-002 в research-notes.md: /jsz-дельты, окно помечать) + минутные пики.
  2. Выход: peak/average/skew per stream; проверка max_bytes против пика, не среднего (NATS Pitfalls: size for busiest).

docs.title: S-4. Week jitter log (Q-006(d); STARTED 2026-09-12, PID 32280)
docs.text:
1. Захват: docker logs -f --timestamps backend-collector-1 → TEMP/jitter-week/collector.log (идёт).
  2. Через неделю: per (symbol, kind) интервалы (<300s флаг) + бакеты (same-bucket doubles флаг) по логу; ground truth — read-only scan_msgids MD_EVENTS (скрипт тогда).
  3. Выход: частота коллизий → вердикт Q-006(d) с числами.

docs.title: S-5. bars-catch-up burst (после первого паблишера)
docs.text: 1. Простой calc >30 мин, рестарт: замерить пачку (N boundaries × символы), поведение discard-old при переполнении BARS, поглощение дубликатов приёмником по (symbol, bar_ts).

docs.title: transition-plan.md — steps 1–2, 4 (free to plan; no product code here)
Step 1. Freeze + converge streams (planner runbook)
docs.text:
1. Freeze subject: bars.binance.usdm.* БЕЗ .30m (код + тест пинят; Q-003d). Заморозка = запись в этот план; смена после — через архитектурное обсуждение (stream recreate + consumers + тесты). TAKE from ADR-0002 C9: точный шаблон тем сырья остаётся md.{market}.{kind}.{symbol} (как в ADR-0001 §8, код уже так пишет) — переезд на md.binance.usdm.<symbol>.<type> НЕ делаем; биржа-в-теме действует только для НОВОГО семейства bars.binance.usdm.*. Механика переезда raw-тем закрыта отказом.
  2. Converge existing MD_: прод-стримы сейчас 72h + max_bytes=-1 (research-notes.md §X-002) — ensure их НЕ сводит (create-only, дрейф log-only). Порядок: (a) снять stream_info снапшот (конфиг целиком); (b) обновить через JetStream update API (retention limits сохранён, меняются max_age/max_bytes) либо delete+recreate пустого BARS; MD_ с данными — только update, НЕ recreate (потеря хвоста); © прогнать check_stream_invariants до зелёного; (d) зафиксировать вывод в ранбук. Откат: update обратно на 72h/unlimited (значения из снапшота (a)).
  3. Owner creation: infra/bootstrap ensure-on-boot идемпотентный (C-2) — каждый boot-путь уже зовёт ensure_and_verify; регрессия: тест с пустой инфры (образец tests/test_book_store_schema_bootstrap.py).

docs.title: Step 2. Shadow archiver (durable+ack, без удаления локального)
docs.text:
1. Новый durable consumer archiver-* на md.* (отдельный от writer-пути; retention limits — чтение несколькими безопасно).
  2. Пишет минутные сегменты (60s + 30s grace, H1–H8) в свой стейджинг-рут; суточное слияние собирает D-002 daily (1 файл/день/тип, все символы) и грузит его в S3 copy-verify-delete; FileWriter'овское локальное НЕ трогает (оно остаётся source of truth; shadow-гейт ARCHIVER_SHADOW_MODE + disjoint-roots проверка fail-loud в archiver/service.py).
  3. Граница файлового диска в тени (Q-005(b)): локально ≤ ~1–2 суток (текущие части + стейджинг слияния); наблюдение — повторный docker system df -v + stream_info (research-notes.md §X-003, абзац «Файлы»), алерт на рост сверх 2 суток.
  4. Критерий выхода из тени: kill-archiver soak (JetStream + файлы): диск стоит, дыра громкая (gap + num_pending), publish не блокируется. Без этого шаг 6 запрещён.
  5. Mixed: двойной диск транзиентно (~2x файлов + JetStream) — входит в границу п.3.

docs.title: Step 4. History consumers to S3/D-002 (backtest + warm-start)
docs.text:
1. Backtest (NG5 offline): ридер на <date>/<type>.parquet (символ — фильтр колонки); оба layout (Hive per-symbol + daily) сосуществуют до миграции; флаг выбора ридера.
  2. Warm-start моста: держать data/metrics пока трейдер in-process; bars/parquet-ридер — только после шага 5.
  3. Миграция Hive→daily: НЕ ТРЕБУЕТСЯ (вердикт человека 2026-09-12 — «забей»). Старая Hive-история остаётся как есть; гейт шага 6 по инструменту миграции СНЯТ (остаются soaks + файловый soak).
  4. Паритет G3: бэктест скипает дыры ровно как live degraded — по штампу (Q-003) как только он есть; до штампа — по bar_complete=false + пропускам ts.

docs.title: Explicitly NOT in this plan (blocked)
docs.text:
• Step 3 (shadow calc с публикацией): ждёт деталей полей Q-003.
  • Step 5 (cutover): ждёт Q-003 + Q-004 build + порядок деплоя уже решён (Q-005: trader/writer stop-first, collector start-first).
  • Step 6 (retire): ждёт soaks + инструмент миграции + файловый soak.

docs.title: Collector and historical data
docs.text:
The live collector publishes Binance events to NATS JetStream. Calc consumes those events to reconstruct books and compute bars. Archiver independently persists the raw feed. Historical ZIP downloads and funding backfills use a separate offline tool.

  • Live collection
  • Historical downloads
  • Storage layout
  • Order-book reconstruction
  • Extending collection

From the repository root:

python -m collector.main live --market usdm --with-funding
python -m collector.tools.history download --market usdm --group major --months 1 --dry-run

docs.title: Extending collection
docs.text:
Add a source at its owning boundary: WebSocket parsing in collector/live/, REST polling in the relevant poller, data schemas in collector/models/, and transport subjects and IDs in common/nats_wire.py.

A new event kind must have a stable deduplication identity, a defined timestamp and a consumer path. Update calc adaptation when metrics use it and archiver serialization when it is persisted. Test parsing, publication and replay with representative payloads. Stream creation must run idempotently in production, not only in test fixtures.

Do not attach a local live file writer or a second metric engine to the collector. Historical data tools use collector/history/downloader/ separately. See architecture and the bars contract.

docs.title: Historical download
docs.text: Pull historical Binance market data from data.binance.vision (ZIP archives) and the REST /fundingRate endpoint, normalised into the same Hive-parquet partition layout used by the archiver. Historical ZIP files and live raw events have different coverage; a ZIP download does not reconstruct live L2.

docs.title: ZIP downloader
docs.text:
python -m collector.tools.history download --market {spot,usdm,both} \
    [--group {all,major}] [--symbols SYM1 SYM2 …] \
    [--types DATA_TYPES …] [--months N] \
    [--intervals INTERVALS …] [--workers W] \
    [--dry-run] [--yes]
Flag What it does --market spot, usdm, or both. URLs differ — see HISTORY_BASES. --group all (601 pairs) or major (top 20). Override with --symbols. --symbols Manual symbol list — bypasses --group. --types Subset of HISTORY_DEFAULT_TYPES: klines, aggTrades, bookTicker. --months How far back to download. Default HISTORY_DEFAULT_MONTHS. --intervals For klines only. Default HISTORY_KLINE_INTERVALS (1m). --workers Parallel download workers. Default HISTORY_DOWNLOAD_WORKERS. --dry-run Print the URL plan and an estimated download size; don't fetch. --yes Skip the size-confirmation prompt.

Always --dry-run first on a wide selection — --group all --months 12 --types klines aggTrades bookTicker is multiple TB.

docs.title: What gets written
docs.text:
data/market={spot|usdm}/type={klines|aggTrades|bookTicker}/
    dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=BTCUSDT/part-monthly[-{interval}].parquet

Note the historical files are monthly chunks (one parquet per symbol per month), partitioned by dt= of the first day of the month. The downloader fans them out into daily dt= partitions on disk to match the live layout — strategies don't see a difference.

The aggTrades history exposes a is_buyer_maker boolean instead of the live stream's pre-flipped side string. The reader's _normalise_columns (metrics/raw_data_reader.py) maps is_buyer_maker → side (True ⇒ "sell", False ⇒ "buy") so the trades aggregator sees a uniform schema.

docs.title: Checkpoint resume
docs.text:
data/.download_checkpoint.json stores completed URLs. A second run skips them, so Ctrl+C / crash mid-batch is safe — re-run with the same arguments and it picks up where it stopped. Checkpoint keys are full URLs, so spot and usdm don't collide.

The checkpoint is per-data-root, so cleaning the data folder also "resets" the checkpoint.

docs.title: Common recipes
docs.text:
# Top-20 USD-M, last 6 months, 1m klines + aggTrades
python -m collector.tools.history download --market usdm --group major \
    --types klines aggTrades --months 6

# All spot pairs, 1 month of bookTicker
python -m collector.tools.history download --market spot --group all \
    --types bookTicker --months 1

# A specific list of symbols, default types, last 3 months
python -m collector.tools.history download --market usdm \
    --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT SOLUSDT --months 3

docs.title: Funding-rate backfill (USD-M only)
docs.text:
The official funding rate endpoint returns one row per settlement (3 per day). Use the history funding subcommand to backfill any window:

python -m collector.tools.history funding [--group {all,major}] \
    [--symbols SYM1 SYM2 …] [--months N] [--dry-run]
Flag What it does --group major (default) or all. Override with --symbols. --symbols Manual list. --months How far back. Default HISTORY_DEFAULT_MONTHS. --dry-run Print the request count; don't hit the endpoint.

Pagination is handled by funding_fetch.py (1000 rows per page, startTime / endTime window). Output:

data/market=usdm/type=funding/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=BTCUSDT/
    part-monthly.parquet

The schema is FundingRateRow: funding_time_ms, symbol, funding_rate (float32), mark_price (float32, optional).

Recipes:

# Backfill a year of funding for the major pairs
python -m collector.tools.history funding --months 12

# Two specific symbols, 6 months
python -m collector.tools.history funding --months 6 --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT

docs.title: Storage cost estimates
docs.text:
Order of magnitude for a single major-pair, 1 month, USD-M:

Type Approx. size klines/1m ~1 MB aggTrades ~50–500 MB (volume-dependent; BTCUSDT is the upper end) bookTicker ~200 MB–2 GB funding <100 KB (3 rows/day)

--dry-run reports the exact upcoming bytes by HEAD-ing each ZIP, so trust the estimate over this table.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• 403 / Not Found — usually a symbol that didn't exist for that month yet. The downloader logs and skips; the batch keeps going.
  • Verify failure — Binance ships per-ZIP .CHECKSUM files; the downloader verifies SHA256. A mismatch is rare and usually means a truncated download. Re-run; the checkpoint won't include it.
  • Pre-existing files — a dt=…/symbol=…/part-monthly.parquet already on disk is treated as complete and skipped (the checkpoint is the source of truth, but the file existence check is a fast fallback).

docs.title: Live collection
docs.text:
collector/services/live.py wires WebSocket listeners and REST pollers to collector/queue_publish.py. Events use the subjects, message IDs and schemas owned by common/nats_wire.py.

Run python -m collector.main live --market usdm --with-funding from the repository root, with NATS connection wiring configured. The collector handles connections, reconnection, publication and its bounded outage buffer. It serves metrics for monitoring; it does not own a live parquet writer.

Calc is the consumer responsible for order-book reconstruction, replay, metric calculation and bar publication. Archiver is an independent durable consumer responsible for raw staging and uploads. The legacy --order-book collector flag is retired.

See architecture, storage and observability.

docs.title: Order-book reconstruction
docs.text:
Calc owns the live L2 book. The collector forwards depth events through NATS; calc applies them, derives metric scalars and persists checkpoints.

On recovery, seed the book from its checkpoint before replaying retained diffs. Ignore diffs already covered by the snapshot and enforce venue-specific update continuity. A gap requires resynchronization; it must not produce a silently incomplete book. Complete historical replay before starting live intake.

The implementation is shared through common/book.py and its consumers; the metric scalar calculation is in metrics/metrics_engine/book_scalars.py. The configured book cadence determines sampling into metric bars. Historical raw-to-metric replay exposes --book-tick-ms through tools/replay_metrics.py.

The current persistence and recovery contract is specified in ADR-0002. Legacy collector snapshot loops are not the production ownership model.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
The live and offline paths use distinct storage contracts.

Data Owner Storage Raw delivery NATS JetStream md.* streams Raw archive Archiver Durable staging, then S3-compatible object storage Live book/checkpoints Calc Memory and Postgres Metric output Calc bars.* publication and metric parquet Trader state Trader Configured state path and Postgres recovery state Historical downloads Historical tool Hive-partitioned parquet

Historical download roots use market=<market>/type=<kind>/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=<symbol>/*.parquet. The readers prune partitions by date and symbol. Historical event schemas live in collector/models/; metric parquet is read through metrics/.

The independent archiver's envelope format and object layout differ from the legacy per-symbol historical download layout. Consumers must use the matching reader rather than assuming that every parquet file has the same schema. Consult ADR-0002 and archiver/ for the durable envelope and upload contract.

The collector does not own live parquet persistence. Precision and timestamp fields are defined by each schema; do not infer one global dtype for raw events, metric bars and book checkpoints.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
For contributors and maintainers.

Page What it covers Setup Local dev environment, virtualenv, optional tools Testing How the test suite is laid out and run Contributing Conventions, PR checklist, commit style

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Follow the repository's AGENTS.md. Keep changes focused on an active caller or a concrete behavior requirement. Prefer a single owner for configuration, transport contracts, persistence and PnL calculations.

docs.title: Code and tests
docs.text:
Use English identifiers and ASCII runtime messages. Do not add code comments or docstrings, except short module help text for offline tools. Explain contracts in design documentation and executable tests. Import at module scope unless a real dependency constraint requires otherwise.

For behavior changes, write a regression test before the implementation and verify both the old failure and new success. Run the relevant suites after finishing edits; testing gives the commands. Keep tests for active behavior when removing dead modules. Infrastructure entities must be created idempotently in production and tested from an empty state.

Trading configuration belongs in live_config.yaml; environment variables hold secrets and service wiring. Invalid required input must fail at its source. Do not introduce alternate PnL kernels or live metric ownership outside calc.

docs.title: Documentation and review
docs.text:
Update current usage documentation alongside behavior and path changes. Preserve historical ADRs and research results as dated records. Report measured research results with data window, method, costs and revision; distinguish synthetic examples from real observations.

A review description should state the problem, resulting behavior and relevant validation. Record any checks that could not run and why. Production deployment and retirement follow the explicit gates in deploy/RUNBOOK.md.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Create a Python 3.13+ virtual environment and install runtime and research dependencies from the repository root:

python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r collector/requirements.txt -r alpha_mining/requirements.txt

Select .venv/bin/python in the editor. Use namespaced package imports such as from collector.models.events import Trade; do not add package-directory import aliases. Offline tools bootstrap the repository root for direct execution.

See testing for the final unit, integration and load checks. A synthetic offline example is:

python tools/backtest.py --mock --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-08 --alphas funding_reversion --no-plot

Documentation tooling is separate from runtime dependencies:

pip install mkdocs-material pymdown-extensions
mkdocs serve
mkdocs build --strict

Repository conventions live in AGENTS.md. Keep service lifecycle in service modules, offline CLI code in tools/, and backtest PnL in its existing kernel.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Run tests from the repository root with the project virtual environment. Complete edits before executing the final checks. For behavior changes, write regression tests first and verify that they fail on the old implementation and pass on the new one.

docs.title: Unit tests
docs.text: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -n auto -m "not slow and not load and not integration and not realdata" --timeout=5

docs.title: Integration tests
docs.text:
Use isolated NATS JetStream and Postgres instances. Set NATS_URL, PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER and PGPASSWORD to those test services. Missing required infrastructure is an error, not a skip. Use a fresh test broker for each integration or slow/load batch: some scenarios intentionally leave streams configured, while the convergence test requires an empty broker.

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -m "integration and not realdata" tests/integration

docs.title: Load and slow tests
docs.text:
Run serially when changing transport, persistence, aggregation or live paths, or when preparing a merge. Do not parallelize timing or memory stress tests.

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -m "(slow or load) and not realdata"

realdata tests require explicitly provisioned datasets. The marker expression on the command line replaces the configured default, so each command above repeats not realdata.

Service tests live beside their package; cross-service tests live under tests/. Keep tests for active contracts when deleting dead implementations. A test exclusively exercising removed code can be removed with it. Infrastructure creation must be tested from an empty database or broker through the production bootstrap path.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Three pages, in order:

  1. Installation — Python 3.13, a venv, dependencies.
  2. Quick start — run a synthetic backtest, then a real one.
  3. Architecture — how the pieces fit together.

If you only have five minutes, jump straight to Quick start.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The live runtime separates ingestion, calculation, execution and archival.

flowchart LR
  Binance --> Collector
  Collector --> Raw["NATS md.*"]
  Raw --> Calc
  Raw --> Archiver
  Calc <--> PG[(Postgres)]
  Calc --> Bars["NATS bars.*"]
  Bars --> Trader
  Trader --> Exchange[Binance execution]
  Trader --> Dashboard
  Archiver --> Storage[Object storage]
Service Owns Collector WebSocket connections, REST pollers, raw publication Calc L2 books, metric engine, checkpoints, closed bars Trader Bar recovery, strategies, allocation, risk and order execution Archiver Durable raw-event staging and object-storage uploads Dashboard Read-only trading views

common/nats_wire.py owns the transport contract. Calc restores its checkpoint, replays retained events, records the recovery outcome, then starts live intake. The trader reads completed metric bars through trader/bars_reader.py; it does not maintain a second live order book or metric engine.

Offline backtests use trader/pipeline.py with raw parquet, precomputed metric parquet or synthetic input. Backtest and live share strategy classes and portfolio logic. All backtest cost and PnL calculations live in trader/backtest/pnl.py.

Trading settings and paths live in live_config.yaml. Environment variables supply credentials and cross-service wiring. See the ADR-0002 for recovery, retention and deployment contracts.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The supported Python baseline is 3.13 or newer. Docker is required for a local full-stack deployment and isolated NATS/Postgres integration tests.

git clone https://github.com/SNCapital/Backend.git backend
cd backend
python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r collector/requirements.txt

Research tools additionally use alpha_mining/requirements.txt. Documentation builds require mkdocs-material and pymdown-extensions.

Start with the offline quick start. See testing for verification commands and required infrastructure. The live stack needs configuration, service connections and credentials; follow deploy/RUNBOOK.md before starting it.

Historical downloads use python -m collector.tools.history from the repository root. Backtests accept their Hive parquet via --data-root, or precomputed metric parquet via --metrics-roots. Match the selected date window and strategy requirements to the available data.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SNCapital/Backend.git backend
cd backend
python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r collector/requirements.txt

docs.title: Run an offline example
docs.text:
python tools/backtest.py --mock --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-08 --alphas funding_reversion --no-plot

This uses synthetic data and prints a performance summary. It does not establish profitability on real market data. Omit --no-plot for the matplotlib dashboard.

For real data, use a raw Hive parquet root with --data-root, or precomputed metric roots with --metrics-roots. Choose dates and strategies for which those roots contain the required data.

Historical-download preview:

python -m collector.tools.history download --market usdm --group major --months 1 --dry-run
python -m collector.tools.history funding --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT --months 12 --dry-run

docs.title: Live runtime
docs.text: Read live trading and deploy/RUNBOOK.md before starting services. The trader reads live_config.yaml, requires the configured NATS/Postgres services and consumes calc's bars. Its configured mode may place real orders; it is not inherently a signal-only demo.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Lookup material — flat lists, tables, glossary entries.

Page What it lists CLI Every flag of python main.py (root) and python collector/main.py Operators All ops in trader/operators.py with signatures and edge cases Metrics catalogue Every metric name data["…"]["…"] accepts, by group Glossary Domain terms — alpha, Sharpe, drawdown, funding, …

If you're looking for narrative documentation (how the pipeline works, how to write a strategy, how to deploy), see the Alpha engine or Binance parser sections.

docs.title: Command-line entry points
docs.text:
Run these commands from the repository root. Use each tool's --help for its current arguments and defaults.

Purpose Command Live bars trader python main.py live-trade Calc service python -m calc Archive service python -m archiver Live collector python -m collector.main live --market usdm --with-funding Historical downloads python -m collector.tools.history download --help Funding backfill python -m collector.tools.history funding --help Backtest python tools/backtest.py --help Raw-to-metric replay python tools/replay_metrics.py --help

Bare python main.py and python main.py live also run the bars trader. Trading settings are read from live_config.yaml; there are no CLI overrides for capital, strategy, symbols or execution mode. Environment variables supply secrets and service connections.

The offline backtester accepts raw parquet (--data-root), precomputed metrics (--metrics-roots) or synthetic data (--mock). --alphas selects registered strategies or research candidates. --execution selects close or next-bar VWAP fills; fees, spread and slippage use the single backtest PnL kernel.

See backtesting, live trading and repository tools/README.md.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Domain terms used throughout the docs. Cross-references in bold.

docs.title: Alpha
docs.text: A signal that, when used as a portfolio weight, generates excess return. Each entry in ALPHA_REGISTRY is one alpha — see Strategies.

docs.title: Bar
docs.text: The base time unit of the engine — 30 minutes UTC-aligned by default. Lookbacks are expressed in bars (48*7 = one week). All strategies operate on bar-frequency DataFrames.

docs.title: Bar clock
docs.text: The async iterator (trader/bar_clock.py) that yields a timestamp at every UTC-aligned bar boundary plus a settlement delay. The live engine's step() runs once per yield.

docs.title: Bid / ask cost
docs.text: USD notional resting on one side of the book within some depth window. bid_25_cost_avg = bar-mean of $-volume of bids within 25% of mid. The base bid_25_cost is expanded into a 9-aggregate suffix pack — see Metrics catalogue.

docs.title: Box constraint
docs.text: A weight bound [min_strategy_weight, max_strategy_weight] enforced during the Markowitz solve. Implemented as water-filling — see Markowitz.

docs.title: Combined weights
docs.text: The output of Layer 3 — what would actually be traded. pipeline.combined_weights is (timestamps × tickers). Computed as \(\sum_k \alpha_{k,t} w_{k,t}\) where \(\alpha_k\) is the Markowitz allocation to strategy \(k\) and \(w_k\) is its per-ticker weight.

docs.title: Cost imbalance
docs.text: (bid_cost - ask_cost) / (bid_cost + ask_cost). Bounded [-1, 1]. Positive = bid-heavy; used by book_depth_imbalance.

docs.title: Drawdown
docs.text: Cumulative PnL minus the running max — always ≤ 0. Reported as max_drawdown in pipeline.summary(). Additive (fraction-of-notional), not percent.

docs.title: End range
docs.text: end_range parameter on AlphaStrategy. Top-N tickers by 30-day rolling USD volume that the strategy is allowed to weight. Default 50. Tickers outside the top-N are NaN'd in the strategy's output.

docs.title: Exchange data
docs.text: metrics.metrics_dict.ExchangeData — top-level dict mapping exchange tag ("binance" / "binance-f") to a lazy AggregatedMetricsDict. The thing strategies receive as self.data.

docs.title: Funding rate
docs.text: USD-M perpetual futures pay periodic funding (every 8h on Binance). Positive funding ⇒ longs pay shorts. Stored as predicted_funding and realized_funding per bar.

docs.title: Gross / net PnL
docs.text:
• Gross — pure price PnL, ignoring fees and funding.
  • Net — gross minus fees plus funding. Closer to what you'd actually realise.

The gross.annualized_sharpe vs. net.annualized_sharpe gap tells you how much the cost model is eating.

docs.title: Hive partitioning
docs.text: Directory layout key1=value1/key2=value2/…/file.parquet that lets a reader prune by partition before opening any file. Used everywhere in data/. See Storage layout.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: The economic story behind an alpha — why it should make money. Each strategy's class docstring is one paragraph stating its hypothesis; fuller version in docs/strategies/<name>.md.

docs.title: Kyle's lambda
docs.text: A regression-slope measure of price impact per unit of order flow. Higher λ ⇒ smaller flows move the price more ⇒ less liquidity. Computed per bar in trades_aggregator.py.

docs.title: Lookback
docs.text: The rolling window length for a feature or for the Markowitz solve. Always in bars.

docs.title: Markowitz / Tobin tangency
docs.text: The closed-form max-Sharpe portfolio \(w^* = \Sigma^{-1}\mu / (\mathbf{1}^\top \Sigma^{-1}\mu)\). Used in Layer 3 to combine strategy "assets". See Markowitz.

docs.title: Mark price
docs.text: USD-M futures' fair-price index. Used for PnL and as a return proxy in strategies (because it's not influenced by venue-specific spreads). Spot has no mark price — close_price plays the role.

docs.title: MarketType
docs.text: Literal["spot", "usdm"] in collector/models/market.py. Maps to the binance / binance-f exchange tags on the alpha-engine side.

docs.title: Metric
docs.text: A (timestamps × tickers) DataFrame that the data layer exposes via data["…"]["…"]. Names listed in Metrics catalogue.

docs.title: MultiFileParquetReader
docs.text: The RawDataReader that knows how to read the parser's Hive layout. Default reader for production backtests.

docs.title: Per-ticker cap
docs.text: max_w parameter on AlphaStrategy. Hard cap on |w_i| per ticker. Default 0.03. Enforced after normalize via trunc_normalize.

docs.title: Quantile (trade)
docs.text: A per-bar percentile threshold on trade size. buy_cost_quantile_0.95 = notional from buys above the 95th percentile of trade size in that bar. Used by trade_imbalance and vol_ob_entropy.

docs.title: Sharpe (annualised)
docs.text: (daily.mean() / daily.std()) * sqrt(365) where daily is bar-PnL resampled to daily. Computed per leg (gross / net).

docs.title: Strategy / alpha
docs.text: Used interchangeably. A class in trader/strategies/alphas.py that subclasses AlphaStrategy and is registered in ALPHA_REGISTRY.

docs.title: Tangency portfolio
docs.text: The point on the efficient frontier with the highest Sharpe ratio (assuming \(r_f = 0\)). Solved in closed form for the strategy combination.

docs.title: Tick
docs.text: A single market event — one trade, one diff, one kline-close. The parser's WebSocket consumer sees a continuous tick stream; the backtest never sees individual ticks (only the per-bar aggregates).

docs.title: JetStream
docs.text: Durable transport between the live services: raw events on md.* and completed metric bars on bars.*. Stream definitions live in common/nats_wire.py.

docs.title: Turnover
docs.text: Sum of per-ticker |Δw| across the day, summed across tickers. Reported as mean_daily_turnover and median_daily_turnover in summary(). Multiply by fee_rate for an order-of-magnitude fee estimate.

docs.title: USD-M
docs.text: Binance's USD-margined perpetual futures venue (fapi.binance.com). Sometimes called "futures" in the codebase. Symbol notation: BTCUSDT (no slash). Funding rates and mark prices live here.

docs.title: Warm-start
docs.text: Restore persisted history and checkpoints before processing live input. Calc replays raw events into its book and metric engine; trader restores completed bars. Recovery must finish before live consumption starts.

docs.title: Water-filling
docs.text: The active-set projection used to enforce box constraints on the tangency portfolio. Pin the worst violator, renormalise the free set along the unconstrained direction, repeat.

docs.title: Metrics catalogue
docs.text: Every key you can pass to data["{exchange}"]["{metric}"]. Generated from the *_METRICS registries in metrics/*_aggregator.py.

docs.title: Klines (klines)
docs.text:
OHLCV data — exists for both spot and USD-M.

Metric Source close_price bar close open_price bar open high_price bar high low_price bar low volume base-asset volume volume_usd quote-asset volume (Binance's quote_volume)

Up to NSC-9 the klines aggregator also exposed mark_price / index_price as aliases of the bar close. They have moved to the markprice kind below — at stress moments the last trade and the real mark price diverge, and the alias was producing false signals.

docs.title: Mark price (markprice)
docs.text:
USD-M only. Sourced from the <symbol>@markPrice@1s WebSocket stream written to data/market=usdm/type=markprice/. The aggregator keeps the last-known value at every 30-min boundary.

Metric Meaning mark_price Real mark price (basis-aware, used for liquidations) index_price Underlying spot index used to compute mark price predicted_funding Predicted rate for the next 8h settlement next_funding_time_ms Settlement timestamp the predicted rate refers to

docs.title: Funding (funding)
docs.text:
USD-M only — realised settlement only. Predicted funding has moved to the markprice kind above.

Metric Meaning realized_funding Last realised settlement rate

docs.title: Trades (trades)
docs.text: Per-bar metrics computed from raw trade-tape ticks. Quantile thresholds q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95} are evaluated per bar on the trade-size distribution. The threshold q is the per-bar percentile — buy_cost_quantile_0.95 sums the notional of buy trades whose own notional is at or above the 95th-percentile of the bar's buy-trade distribution (i.e. the top ~5% by size).

docs.title: Aggregates
docs.text: Metric Meaning volume Total base-asset volume in the bar buy_volume Volume from aggressor-buy trades sell_volume Volume from aggressor-sell trades buy_cost Notional ($) of aggressor-buy trades sell_cost Notional ($) of aggressor-sell trades buy_count Number of aggressor-buy trades sell_count Number of aggressor-sell trades vwap Volume-weighted average price buy_vwap VWAP across buy trades only sell_vwap VWAP across sell trades only open / close / high / low OHLC from trades (not the kline), averaged across buy/sell volatility Intra-bar std of minute log-returns (ddof=1, NaN if <3 non-empty minutes) hh Herfindahl index of trade-size concentration hh_buy Same, restricted to buys hh_sell Same, restricted to sells kyle_lambda Kyle's lambda (price impact regression slope on log-returns) max_buy_trade_cost Largest single buy trade ($) max_sell_trade_cost Largest single sell trade ($) asr_count Adverse-selection ratio by count (60s cross-bar lookahead) asr_volume Adverse-selection ratio by volume

docs.title: Count-above-threshold — T ∈ {100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000}
docs.text:
For each USD threshold T:

Metric pattern Meaning buy_count_above_T Number of buy trades with notional strictly > T sell_count_above_T Same for sells

docs.title: Quantile metrics — q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95}
docs.text:
For each q:

Metric pattern Meaning buy_cost_quantile_{q} USD notional sum from buys at or above the q-th percentile by notional sell_cost_quantile_{q} Same for sells buy_trade_cost_quantile_{q} The q-th percentile boundary itself (single value, USD) sell_trade_cost_quantile_{q} Same for sells buy_volume_quantile_{q}_usd Alias of buy_cost_quantile_{q} (v1-bridge) sell_volume_quantile_{q}_usd Same buy_volume_quantile_{q} Base-asset volume version sell_volume_quantile_{q} Same buy_count_quantile_{q} Number of buys above the q-th percentile sell_count_quantile_{q} Same volume_quantile_{q} / _usd Overall volume version (no side) count_quantile_{q} Overall count version (no side)

So data["binance-f"]["buy_cost_quantile_0.95"] is the per-bar USD spent by aggressor-buys whose own notional is at or above the 95th-percentile of the bar's buy distribution.

docs.title: Trades multilevel (trades_multilevel)
docs.text:
Per-bar metrics computed on logical trades — chains of contiguous raw fills that share side, timestamp, and consecutive trade_ids with monotonic price. Suffix _ml = multilevel (chain length ≥ 2), _sl = single-level (chain length = 1).

Quantile threshold q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95}. 73 keys total.

Metric pattern Meaning {buy,sell}_count_{ml,sl} Chain counts per side {buy,sell}_cost_{ml,sl} Chain notional totals mean_cost_{ml,sl} Mean cost per chain (overall) {buy,sell}_vwap_{ml,sl} VWAP across chains, per side {buy,sell}_cost_quantile_{q}_{ml,sl} Top-q sums of chain notionals {buy,sell}_trade_cost_quantile_{q}_{ml,sl} q-th percentile boundary {buy,sell}_mean_price_delta_ml_quantile_{q} Mean (price_last − price_first) / price_first × side_sign for chains above q, ml only

Identity invariant (pinned by tests): buy_cost == buy_cost_ml + buy_cost_sl.

docs.title: Orderbook (orderbook)
docs.text: Snapshot-based, multi-aggregated across the bar's snapshots. Depth percentages d ∈ {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100} are percent-of-mid — bid_25_cost_avg is the bar-mean of bid liquidity within 25% of the running mid. Underscores in metric names come from str.replace(".", "_"), so 0.5 becomes 0_5.

docs.title: Aggregation suffix packs
docs.text:
Each per-snapshot base metric is expanded into one of two packs:

  • 9-agg pack (_avg, _quantile_25, _quantile_50, _quantile_75, _quantile_90, _quantile_95, _skew, _min, _max): drops NaN samples only. Used for level / state metrics.
  • 10-agg pack (= 9-agg + _sum): additionally drops zero samples. Used for cross-snapshot diff / log-return metrics where 0 means "no observation".

docs.title: Best level (9-agg)
docs.text: Base metric Pack best_bid_price 9-agg best_ask_price 9-agg best_bid_size 9-agg best_ask_size 9-agg bid_ask_spread_abs 9-agg — absolute spread best_ask − best_bid bid_ask_spread_rel 9-agg — relative spread spread / mid last_best_bid_price last snapshot in the bar (scalar) last_best_ask_price last snapshot in the bar (scalar)

docs.title: Per-depth metrics (9-agg)
docs.text:
For each depth d, side s ∈ {bid, ask}:

Base metric Meaning {s}_{d}_cost USD notional within d% of mid on side s {s}_{d}_size Base-asset size within d% of mid {s}_{d}_vwap VWAP of liquidity within d% {s}_{d}_levels_size_count Number of populated levels within d% {s}_{d}_levels_size_count_nonzero Count of levels with size > 0 {s}_{d}_levels_size_mean Mean size per level within d% cost_imbalance_{d}_ratio (bid_cost − ask_cost) / (bid_cost + ask_cost) cost_imbalance_{d}_norm Normalised variant: 1.0 if ask_cost = 0, NaN if both = 0 vwap_{d}_midprice (bid_vwap + ask_vwap) / 2 per snapshot

docs.title: Cross-snapshot diff / log-return (10-agg)
docs.text: Base metric Meaning {s}_{d}_cost_diff Δ cost vs. previous snapshot {s}_{d}_size_diff Δ size vs. previous snapshot {s}_{d}_price_logreturn log-return of cumulative VWAP best_{s}_size_diff Δ best-level size best_{s}_price_logreturn log-return of best price

docs.title: Liquidity-shock — d ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 5, 25, 50} (9-agg)
docs.text:
liq_shock_{side}_{d} = {side}_{d}_size[t] / rolling_mean(10s of {side}_{d}_size).

Base metric Meaning liq_shock_bid_{d} Bid-side instantaneous liquidity vs 10s baseline liq_shock_ask_{d} Ask-side liq vs baseline liq_shock_ratio_{d} liq_shock_bid / (liq_shock_bid + liq_shock_ask)

docs.title: Liquidations (liquidations)
docs.text:
Per-bar metrics on liquidation fills, prefixed liquidations_. Reader maps cum_filled_qty → size, avg_price → price (per fill, not the order intent), then filters size > 0. Same algorithmic template as trades — 50 keys total. Examples:

Metric Meaning liquidations_{buy,sell}_count Count of long/short liquidations liquidations_{buy,sell}_count_above_{T} T ∈ liquidations_{buy,sell}_cost Notional sums liquidations_{buy,sell}_cost_quantile_{q} q ∈ liquidations_max_{buy,sell}_trade_cost Largest single liquidation ($) liquidations_vwap, _buy_vwap, _sell_vwap VWAPs liquidations_open/high/low/close OHLC, NaN if either side empty liquidations_volatility Intra-bar minute log-return std liquidations_hh, _hh_buy, _hh_sell HH on size (per L_T2.8) liquidations_kyle_lambda Kyle's lambda liquidations_asr_count, _asr_volume 60s cross-bar lookahead

docs.title: Maker orders (maker_orders)
docs.text:
Spot-only (Binance spot). Each raw trade reconstructs to one maker_fill with the maker side inverted from taker: taker BUY → maker ASK, taker SELL → maker BID. ASR sign convention is inverted vs. taker (ask-maker "wins" when price falls).

Prefix maker_ everywhere — deliberate deviation from generic bid_*/ask_* to avoid namespace collision with orderbook. 50 keys with the same structural template as trades/liquidations. Examples:

Metric Meaning maker_{ask,bid}_count Maker fills counted on each side maker_{ask,bid}_count_above_{T} T ∈ maker_{ask,bid}_cost_quantile_{q} q ∈ maker_max_{ask,bid}_trade_cost Largest single maker fill ($) maker_vwap, maker_ask_vwap, maker_bid_vwap Maker-side VWAPs maker_volatility, maker_kyle_lambda Identical algos to taker template maker_asr_count, maker_asr_volume 60s lookahead, sign inverted

Identity invariants (pinned): maker_ask_cost == buy_cost, maker_bid_cost == sell_cost, maker_vwap == vwap.

docs.title: Market stats (market_stats)
docs.text:
USD-M only. Polled via REST (Binance futures + spot margin endpoints), not WebSocket. Futures coroutine runs at 5-min UTC-aligned cadence; spot interest at 1h cadence. Aggregator does resample("30min").last() .ffill().reindex(idx).ffill().

Metric Source endpoint open_interest /fapi/v1/openInterest global_long_accounts /futures/data/globalLongShortAccountRatio top_long_accounts /futures/data/topLongShortAccountRatio top_long_positions /futures/data/topLongShortPositionRatio daily_interest_rate /sapi/v1/margin/next-hourly-interest-rate × 24 (linear, no compounding). Gated MARGIN_INTEREST_ENABLED, opt-in.

docs.title: How resolution works
docs.text:
The lazy dict (AggregatedMetricsDict) maps a metric name to an aggregator group via prefix rules in metrics_dict._resolve_source:

Prefix / pattern Group liquidations_* liquidations maker_* maker_orders {open_interest, global_long_*, top_long_*, daily_interest_rate} market_stats *_ml / *_sl / mean_cost_{ml,sl} / *_mean_price_delta_ml_* trades_multilevel bid_* or ask_* containing cost / size / vwap / levels / spread / logreturn orderbook cost_imbalance_*, vwap_*_midprice, liq_shock_*, last_best_* orderbook buy_* or sell_* trades close_price, volume_usd, … klines mark_price, index_price, next_funding_time_ms, predicted_funding markprice anything else containing funding funding

Names that don't match raise KeyError — the dict refuses to guess. To add a new metric whose name doesn't fit, also add a branch in _resolve_source.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Lightweight building blocks in trader/operators.py. Use these in gen_weights_raw — they handle the NaN / divide-by-zero cases that bite on real data.

from trader.operators import (
    rank, normalize, trunc_normalize, norm_ratio,
    ts_return, ts_logreturn, ts_ema, ts_std, ts_zscore,
    set_entropy, set_mean,
)

docs.title: rank(df) → df
docs.text:
Per-row percentile rank in [0, 1]. Implemented as df.rank(axis=1, pct=True). NaN rows stay NaN.

rank(pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3, 4]])).values
# array([[0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00]])

docs.title: normalize(df) → df
docs.text:
Per-row demean, then scale so |w|.sum() == 1.

df  := df - df.mean(axis=1)
df  := df / df.abs().sum(axis=1).replace(0, NaN)

A row of all-equal values goes to all-zeros (after demean) → divide-by- zero is replaced with NaN, the row stays NaN.

docs.title: trunc_normalize(df, max_w) → df
docs.text:
normalize, then clip(-max_w, max_w). Does not re-normalise after the clip — by design. The base strategy class uses this to enforce a per-ticker cap; the resulting weights are no longer exactly abs-sum-1 but the cap is hard.

If you'd rather re-normalise (preserve abs-sum-1, sacrifice the cap), do normalize(trunc_normalize(df, max_w)).

docs.title: norm_ratio(a, b) → df
docs.text:
(a - b) / (a + b). Bounded in [-1, 1] for non-negative inputs. NaN where a + b == 0.

The de-facto "imbalance" operator — used in book_depth_imbalance, trade_imbalance, vol_ob_entropy.

docs.title: set_entropy(*dfs) → df
docs.text:
Shannon-like entropy across a set of DataFrames, treating each one as a share after normalisation:

total := Σ |df_k|
p_k   := |df_k| / total
H     := -Σ p_k · log(p_k)

NaN entries (zero share) are skipped — entropy is computed only over non-zero shares. Result is filled with 0 where the entire row was NaN.

Used in vol_ob_entropy to measure concentration of trade-volume across quantile bins vs. concentration of book depth across bid/ask.

docs.title: set_mean(*dfs) → df
docs.text: Element-wise NaN-aware mean across a set of DataFrames. Same shape; preserves index/columns.

docs.title: Time-series
docs.text: All time-series ops use min_periods=1 so they don't produce a full NaN warmup — they grow into their window.

docs.title: ts_return(df, periods=1) → df
docs.text: Simple return: df.pct_change(periods).

docs.title: ts_logreturn(df, periods=1) → df
docs.text: log(df / df.shift(periods)). Same warmup as ts_return.

docs.title: ts_ema(df, span) → df
docs.text: Exponential moving average: df.ewm(span=span, min_periods=1).mean(). The span / decay convention is pandas' standard (alpha = 2/(span+1)).

docs.title: ts_std(df, window) → df
docs.text: Rolling standard deviation: df.rolling(window, min_periods=1).std(). The first row is NaN (std of a single point is undefined).

docs.title: ts_zscore(df, window) → df
docs.text:
Rolling z-score:

mean := df.rolling(window, min_periods=1).mean()
std  := df.rolling(window, min_periods=1).std().replace(0, NaN)
z    := (df - mean) / std

std == 0 (e.g. constant window) → NaN, not Inf.

The standard "normalise across recent history" tool. Z-score before EMA is a common pattern across the strategy registry.

docs.title: ts_slope(df, window) → df
docs.text:
Rolling linear-trend slope: cov(y, t) / var(t) over the window, where t is the bar index (0, 1, 2, ...). Positive = trending up over the window, negative = trending down — a directional-trend counterpart to ts_ema (smoothing, no direction) and ts_zscore (level, no trend).

Implemented against a global bar index rather than re-basing t to 0..window-1 inside every window: covariance and variance are shift-invariant (cov(y, t+k) == cov(y, t) for any constant k), and any rolling window of a strictly-increasing-by-1 sequence is just a shifted copy of 0..window-1 — so the global index gives the exact same slope as a per-window re-based one, fully vectorised (no per-window Python loop, no rolling().apply(...)).

docs.title: ts_regress_residual(y, x, window) → df
docs.text:
Rolling OLS residual of y regressed on x, per column:

mean_y, mean_x := rolling means of y, x (window)
cov  := rolling_mean(y*x) - mean_y*mean_x
var_x:= rolling_mean(x*x) - mean_x**2, replace(0, NaN)
beta := cov / var_x
alpha:= mean_y - beta*mean_x
resid:= y - (alpha + beta*x)

x may be:

  • a DataFrame the same shape as y — pairwise per-column regression. This is Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization: ts_regress_residual(signal_b, signal_a, window) returns the part of signal_b not explained by signal_a, useful for building a genuinely incremental signal on top of an established one instead of an accidentally-correlated variant.
  • a Series — broadcast to every column of y. The standard use is residualizing each ticker's return against a single market/equal-weight return series to get idiosyncratic (beta-neutral) returns before momentum/reversal, rather than a simple cross-sectional demean (which only removes the mean, not each name's own market-beta exposure).

var(x) == 0 (e.g. a constant regressor) → NaN, not Inf, matching ts_zscore's convention.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text: You want… Use… A bounded [-1, 1] signal from two non-negative series norm_ratio A bounded [0, 1] signal from raw values across the universe rank To turn a raw signal into dollar-neutral weights normalize (then trunc_normalize for the cap) To measure concentration / dispersion across quantile bins set_entropy To smooth a signal ts_ema (span = how many bars of "memory") To remove level / drift from a metric ts_zscore (window = "what counts as recent") To compute returns ts_return (or ts_logreturn if you'll sum across time) Rolling vol ts_std(ts_return(price, 1), window) To measure directional trend (not just level) ts_slope To remove another signal's (or the market's) influence before trading the remainder ts_regress_residual

docs.title: NSC-14 backfill — aggTrade vs trade trade-off table (NSC-42)
docs.text:
NSC-14 (PR #15, commit 1c95f7a) switched the canonical trade source to @aggTrade-only and stopped subscribing to raw @trade. The decision was sound but the research phase was skipped — there was no side-by-side numbers table comparing the three options. This page is the post-hoc backfill so the choice is reproducible from numbers, not just narrative.

Status: the choice is merged and not under reconsideration. This doc exists for auditability.

docs.title: The three options
docs.text:
• Option A — aggTrades-only (chosen). Subscribe only to @aggTrade, treat type=aggtrades (live) and type=aggTrades (historical archive) as the single canonical kind="trades" source.
  • Option B — raw trades-only. Subscribe only to @trade, store type=trades only. Historical parity requires re-aggregating from the aggTrades archive (the archive does not ship raw trades).
  • Option C — both, dedup downstream. Subscribe to both streams, write both partition types, and add a deduplication step in the reader so each fill is counted exactly once.

docs.title: Measured numbers — 5-min capture, BTCUSDT + ETHUSDT, spot
docs.text:
Synthetic data

Numbers below are SYNTHETIC — generated through the real binance_parser DTOs and FileWriter because the egress proxy blocks Binance hosts. See How the numbers were collected for the full disclosure and reproducer.

symbol type files size (MB) rows $ volume BTCUSDT trades 1 0.1134 9,000 8,966,001 BTCUSDT aggtrades 1 0.0495 2,571 8,966,001 ETHUSDT trades 1 0.0667 5,400 4,181,993 ETHUSDT aggtrades 1 0.0349 1,800 4,181,993

Per-symbol compression (raw vs aggregated, same window):

  • BTCUSDT — 3.50× fewer rows, 2.29× smaller on-disk after zstd-3.
  • ETHUSDT — 3.00× fewer rows, 1.91× smaller on-disk after zstd-3.

Dollar volume sums are identical to the dollar by construction — aggTrade preserves total executed notional, it only collapses same-side same-price fills inside a 100 ms bucket on Binance's side.

docs.title: How the numbers were collected
docs.text:
Live capture was attempted via the parser's WebSocket path (binance_parser/main.py live --market spot --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT with LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES=False patched in for the run) and the historical archive (history download … --types aggTrades trades). Both routes failed inside the worktree's network: the egress proxy returned 403 host_not_allowed for data.binance.vision, api.binance.com, and stream.binance.com:9443. No pre-existing parquet partitions are checked into the repo.

Because a real 5-minute capture was infeasible, the rows above were generated by a synthetic driver (/tmp/synth_nsc42.py) that:

  1. Constructs Trade and AggTrade DTOs from binance_parser/models/events.py directly — same dataclass, same pa.Schema, same to_rows() shape.
  2. Pushes them through the real live.writer.FileWriter, so on-disk layout, parquet writer settings, and zstd-3 compression match the live path byte-for-byte (PARQUET_COMPRESSION = "zstd", PARQUET_COMPRESSION_LEVEL = 3).
  3. Calibrates per-symbol rates from publicly-cited 2024 BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT spot activity: BTCUSDT ≈ 30 raw trades/s, ETHUSDT ≈ 18 raw trades/s, aggregation factors 3.5× / 3.0× respectively (well within the 2–5× range Binance publishes).

The output was measured with pyarrow.dataset.dataset(...).to_table(...) summing price * qty and os.stat().st_size over the partition files.

Caveats that matter for an audit reviewer:

  • File-size figures are realistic relative to each other (same writer, same compression) but absolute numbers will differ from a real Binance capture by whatever the synthetic price/qty distribution misses (zstd compresses repeated prices and timestamps very well — real BTCUSDT bursts have higher repetition and would compress more, so the aggTrade size advantage is, if anything, understated here).
  • Aggregation ratios are deterministic in the synthetic data; in production they vary minute-to-minute (3–5× is normal, can spike to

    10× during quiet periods or drop near 1× during one-sided cascades).

  • Dollar-volume parity between trades and aggTrades is exact in the synthetic capture (the aggregator preserves Σ price·qty); on the live feed it is also exact up to float32 rounding — @aggTrade is a lossless bucketing on Binance's side.

docs.title: What the numbers say
docs.text:
• Storage — Option A is ~2.0–2.3× cheaper on disk than Option B and ~3.0–3.5× cheaper than Option C, at the same dollar volume. For 601 symbols × 30 days the difference compounds to multi-GB savings.
  • Schema parity — Option A is the only one with native archive parity: data.binance.vision ships aggTrades shards but no raw-trade shards for spot daily, so backtest and live read the same bucketing of fills with no re-aggregation step.
  • Information loss — Option A loses per-fill granularity (queue position, microstructure-level trade-id sequencing). For the alpha set in ALPHA_REGISTRY today (trade_imbalance and friends operating on 30-min bars) that loss is invisible — the aggregator preserves signed notional and signed count by side. For future microstructure-level work the reader can be flipped back to Option C via LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES=False.
  • Operational risk — Option C requires a dedup step on every read; a bug there silently double-counts notional and fakes higher signal strength. Option A has no such failure mode.

docs.title: Conclusion (post-hoc)
docs.text: Option A is the right choice given the current alpha set: it is cheaper to store, has clean archive parity, and removes a class of dedup bugs. The information lost is recoverable on demand — set LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES=False to re-enable raw @trade capture for any future microstructure work (type=trades partitions still write through the same FileWriter; the alpha engine reader still ignores them to avoid double-counting).

docs.title: Reproducing
docs.text:
To re-run on a host with Binance egress, use the parser's own CLI for a fresh 5-min sample with both streams subscribed:

# Temporarily flip the canonical trade switch so both partitions get written.
export LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES=False    # not yet env-driven; for now patch
                                      # binance_parser/config/settings.py:72
cd binance_parser
timeout 300 python main.py live --market spot --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT

Then point the measurement script at the resulting binance_parser/data/ tree:

import pyarrow.dataset as ds
from pathlib import Path

DATA = Path("binance_parser/data/market=spot")
for typ in ("trades", "aggtrades"):
    for sym in ("BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT"):
        files = list((DATA / f"type={typ}").rglob(f"symbol={sym}/*.parquet"))
        size_mb = sum(p.stat().st_size for p in files) / (1024**2)
        t = ds.dataset([str(p) for p in files], format="parquet").to_table(
            columns=["price", "qty"]
        )
        rows = t.num_rows
        dvol = float((t["price"].to_numpy() * t["qty"].to_numpy()).sum())
        print(f"{sym:8s} {typ:10s} {len(files):3d} files  {size_mb:8.4f} MB  "
              f"{rows:>10,} rows  ${dvol:>16,.0f}")

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text: One file per alpha. Each describes the steady-state design — hypothesis, signal, data inputs, parameters. Measured numbers (Sharpe, drawdown, turnover) live in the Research log, tagged with a date and data range.

docs.title: Index
docs.text: File ALPHA_REGISTRY key Hypothesis Primary data Orderbook mispricing ob_mispricing Limit-order book lags last trade price → momentum continues Spot L2 + futures mark Volume / OB entropy vol_ob_entropy Concentrated trade flow vs. symmetric book = informed flow Futures L2 + trade-size quantiles Funding mean reversion funding_reversion Extreme funding rates revert USD-M funding Trade imbalance trade_imbalance Big buys vs. big sells (top quantile) is informative Futures large-trade volume Volatility mean reversion vol_mean_reversion Low-vol regimes break out in the direction of recent drift Futures mark price Book depth imbalance book_depth_imbalance Asymmetric book depth at 25% predicts drift Futures L2 cost @ 25%

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• One strategy = one file. Filename matches the strategy's name in ALPHA_REGISTRY (e.g. funding_reversion.md).
  • Code-derived sections (signal formula, parameters) should match the current trader/strategies/alphas.py. If you change the code, update the doc in the same commit.
  • Numbers (Sharpe, drawdown, turnover) belong in research-log.md with a date and the commit / data range they were measured against — not in the per-strategy file, which describes the steady-state design.

docs.title: File template
docs.text:
Every per-strategy file follows the same shape:

# <Display name> (`<registry_key>`)

## Hypothesis
## Signal
## Data inputs
## Parameters
## Caveats / known weaknesses

Adding a new strategy: copy funding_reversion.md, fill the sections, add a row to the table above, register the class in ALPHA_REGISTRY. Walk-through: Writing a strategy.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: When bid depth at 25% is much larger than ask depth, there's a "wall" of support. Price is less likely to crash and more likely to drift up. The book shows where passive capital is positioned.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
raw     = norm_ratio(bid_25_cost_avg, ask_25_cost_avg)
signal  = ts_zscore(raw, window=48*7)             # 7-day z-score
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*3)               # 3-day EMA

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text: Source Field USD-M bid_25_cost_avg (bar-mean of notional resting on the bid within 25% of mid) USD-M ask_25_cost_avg

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Book depth: 25% of mid (cost-integrated).
  • z-score window: 48 * 7.
  • EMA span: 48 * 3.

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• Layered / spoofed orders inflate visible depth without representing real intent — the book can lie.
  • 25% is a wide band; sensitivity vs. tighter (e.g. 5% / 10%) bands hasn't been logged here.
  • Strongly correlated with ob_mispricing — Markowitz combination should diversify them away, but watch the strategy correlation matrix.
  • From research doc: imbalance decay, layering filter.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: Extreme funding rates revert. When funding is very positive, longs are paying shorts heavily — the market is overleveraged long, and price tends to drop. Vice versa for very negative funding.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
signal  = -ts_zscore(predicted_funding, window=48*14)   # 14-day z-score
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*3)                     # 3-day EMA

The z-score normalises across the per-ticker funding distribution; the negative sign turns "expensive to be long" into a short.

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text:
Source Field USD-M predicted_funding

Realised funding is also consumed by the PnL leg (compute_pnl(funding=...)) — see ../methodology.md.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• z-score window: 48 * 14 (two weeks of 30-min bars).
  • EMA span: 48 * 3 (three days).

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• Funding settles every 8h — at the bar level the predicted-funding series steps rather than evolves smoothly. The 3-day EMA is the main smoother.
  • "Extreme" is defined by the rolling 2-week distribution per ticker; regime shifts (BTC funding regime in bull vs. flat market) can mute the signal.
  • From research doc: regime sensitivity, funding-reversion vs. carry.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: Limit-order traders in the book are slower than the market. When the volume-weighted mid-price in the book lags behind the last trade price, the book hasn't caught up yet — price will continue in the same direction.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
ob_mid = (bid_25_vwap_avg + ask_25_vwap_avg) / 2  # spot, bar-mean of per-snapshot VWAPs
signal = -(ob_mid / mark_price)                   # futures mark
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*5)               # 5-day EMA

Negative sign: "book is behind, momentum will continue".

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text:
Source Field Spot bid_25_vwap_avg, ask_25_vwap_avg (bar-mean of book VWAP at 25% depth) USD-M mark_price

Cross-venue: spot book vs. futures mark. Requires both feeds in MetricsDict.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• EMA span: 48 * 5 (5 days of 30-min bars).
  • Per-ticker cap max_w = 0.03, top-end_range = 50 by volume.

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• Spot book ≠ futures execution venue: basis moves (cash-and-carry, funding) bleed into the signal as noise.
  • 25% depth VWAP can be thin for small-cap pairs.
  • From research doc: validate on rolling windows.
